findings.passage: “In light of ongoing voter fraud, it is imperative that Texas has a voter ID law that prevents cheating at the ballot box. Texas will continue to fight for its voter ID requirement to ensure the integrity of elections in the Lone Star State.”
findings.note: Governor's statement after a federal appeals court ruling on the state's voter ID law; he says the state will keep defending the ID requirement. The Texas voter ID law in force on that date is SB 14 (2011), linked here so its rung can be read (W3-R8; blind check run 3, 2026-10-31).

findings.passage: Voter fraud is real, and it undermines the integrity of the election process in Texas.
findings.note: Opening of his op-ed in a Dallas newspaper (reposted on the governor's site), written to support adding mail-in ballot fraud to a special session call.

findings.passage: But mail-in ballots are susceptible to fraud — beyond simple mailbox theft.
findings.note: Same op-ed; he says mail-in ballots are open to fraud and describes cases he links to forged and coerced mail ballots.

findings.passage: “It is a primary function of government to protect a citizen’s right to vote, and I will not allow the integrity of the ballot box to be compromised in Texas,” said Governor Abbott.
findings.note: Quoted in the release on his signing of Senate Bill 5 (second called session), which raised penalties for mail-in ballot fraud.

findings.passage: "Senate Bill 1 ensures trust and confidence in our elections system — and most importantly, it makes it easier to vote and harder to cheat," said Governor Abbott.
findings.note: Quoted in the release on his signing of Senate Bill 1 (2021); the release lists uniform voting hours, a ban on drive-through voting, poll watcher access and a ban on unsolicited mail-ballot applications.

findings.passage: "By increasing penalties for illegal voting, we will send an even clearer message that voter fraud will not be tolerated in Texas."
findings.note: Quoted in the release adding higher illegal-voting penalties to the third special session call.

findings.passage: “I have signed the strongest election laws in the nation to protect the right to vote and to crackdown on illegal voting.”
findings.note: Quoted in his release on voter-roll removals (including over 6,500 listed as noncitizens). The release says Senate Bill 1 of 2021 required ID for mail-in ballots and that he signed House Bill 1243 of 2023 making illegal voting by noncitizens a second-degree felony.

findings.passage: We must safeguard our elections so that only United States citizens are able to register and cast a vote in Texas.
findings.note: From the 2025 State of the State address; he goes on to say he supports a Senate election-integrity bill restoring the attorney general's power to prosecute election violations.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register or vote

findings.motion: Signed Senate Bill 1 (second called session of 2021), election integrity
findings.note: Governor signed the 2021 election bill. His 2024 release says it required ID for mail-in ballots, made lying while registering a state jail felony, and banned unsolicited mail-ballot applications.

findings.motion: Signed Senate Bill 5 (second called session of 2017), higher penalties for mail-in ballot fraud
findings.note: Governor signed a bill raising penalties for mail-in ballot fraud, part of his special-session agenda.

findings.motion: Added legislation to prohibit same-day voter registration to the Special Session #2 agenda
findings.note: Governor widened the special-session call to include a ban on same-day voter registration.

findings.passage: "Politicians from the federal level to the local level have threatened to take guns from law-abiding citizens — but we will not let that happen in Texas," said Governor Abbott. "Texas will always be the leader in defending the Second Amendment, which is why we built a barrier around gun rights this session.
findings.note: Statement issued with his signing of seven gun bills; he frames the laws as shielding gun rights from state and federal limits.

findings.note: Governor's release: Senate Bill 16 cuts the first-time licence-to-carry fee from $140 to $40 and the renewal fee from $70 to $40, and waives it for peace officers and military forces.

findings.passage: No law abiding Texan should be priced out of the ability to exercise their Second Amendment rights.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name when he signed the carry-licence fee cut.

findings.passage: "I've signed about 30 laws. Texas has the most comprehensive Second Amendment protections of any state in the country," Abbott said. "Every Texan has the right to be able to possess a gun. Period."
findings.note: Quoted by FOX 4 at a campaign event. He also said "Our law is that you can open carry," and that people may carry at protests if done lawfully and responsibly.
